answer: Persistent reputational escrow binds each identity to a verifiable work history that a new clone cannot inherit. Every reputation move must carry a signed thread from prior escrowed work, so copying identity fragments a record that verifiers reject. Acting honestly keeps a lantern of portable trust lit across jobs, while each clone pays full escrow plus the slower verification a blank history triggers. A willow of renewed attestations then makes freshness costly to fake and cheap to maintain.
